A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IG-AE research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeRF training, novel-view synthesis, autoencoder reconstruction, ablation, and timing results in Tables 1–5 and associated figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds latent-space evaluations, synthetic reconstruction results, an autoencoder-resolution study, and further Objaverse evaluations.

M1.justification: The two-stage latent NeRF pipeline, joint autoencoder/Tri-Plane training, 3D regularization, reconstruction objectives, and TV regularization remain unchanged. The additional autoencoder configurations are an experimental design study, not a revision of IG-AE.

E1.justification: v2 Table 7 extends reconstruction evaluation from held-out ImageNet images to held-out Objaverse and out-of-distribution ShapeNet images. NVS retains the same synthetic object domains and dataset families; the additional Objaverse objects expand sampling within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The AE, IG-AE, ablated IG-AE, and RGB comparisons retain the same participating NeRF architectures. v2 Table 3 compares related work descriptively, without evaluating those methods. Table 9 studies unregularized autoencoder configurations rather than adding competitors evaluated against IG-AE.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation protocols: PSNR/SSIM between rendered and encoded latent images (Table 6), synthetic reconstruction averaged over test-scene images (Table 7), and a kl-f4/kl-f8/kl-f16 configuration comparison (Table 9). These substantially broaden the evaluation design. The original experiments retain their reported training budgets and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: v2 adds a latent-space diagnostic testing how well NeRFs reproduce encoded images and a systematic autoencoder-resolution sensitivity study across four NeRF architectures. These examine latent compatibility and the resolution choice beyond v1's component-removal and RGB-alignment ablations, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing scene averages and timing averages over 1,000 renderings remain; additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained numerical tables are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 6, 7, and 9–14, including 15 additional Objaverse objects. For example, Table 6 newly reports Cake latent PSNR of 38.36 for AE versus 50.31 for IG-AE with Vanilla-NeRF. Table 7 reports improved synthetic reconstruction PSNR/SSIM but worse LPIPS. These are additional comparisons, not revisions of v1's performance values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–14 are unchanged, including 3D consistency, training losses, and TV regularization. The Tri-Plane appendix moves from Appendix A to C; no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and five principal contributions retain the same scientific scope: a 3D-aware autoencoder, latent NeRF training, Nerfstudio integration, improved quality over a standard AE, and efficiency relative to RGB training. v2's more explicit novelty wording restates claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v1 already acknowledges lost high-frequency detail. v2 Section 5.4 adds a speculative low-frequency regularization explanation and explicitly connects this limitation to complex real-world scenes. Appendix E adds a locality-based explanation for resolution sensitivity, while Appendix D.2 interprets the synthetic reconstruction LPIPS tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix B provides direct repository addresses for the Nerfstudio extension and IG-AE training, replacing v1's less concrete release statement. Existing hardware, training times, and hyperparameters are retained after relocation. However, v2 omits v1's explicit spherical camera-pose sampling description and statement that evaluation scenes share the training rendering resolution and view count.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds scene-embedding research, and new Appendix A provides a substantial comparison of rendering spaces, tasks, and representations. Added works include NeRF-VAE, RODIN, LN3Diff, StyleNeRF, and LERF. The discussion more explicitly distinguishes IG-AE from generation, feature distillation, editing, and hybrid RGB/latent reconstruction. References to Ramesh et al. and Kassab et al. are removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: introductory motivation is expanded, implementation and training subsections move from the experiments section to Appendix B, limitations receive a dedicated subsection, and the appendices are reorganized around related work, implementation, analyses, and hyperparameters. The central method exposition remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds a related-work comparison matrix, eight empirical tables, and five qualitative figures. Existing tables and figures are retained but relocated, resized, or repacked, including the appendix reconstruction examples and hyperparameter tables. This is a substantial display expansion beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central latent-space claim through direct latent NVS measurements, resolution sensitivity analysis, and comparisons on 15 additional held-out objects. Synthetic reconstruction results also expose a perceptual-quality tradeoff. Expanded research positioning, clearer applicability limits, and explicit code-access information make the contribution easier to assess and reproduce. These gains outweigh the limited loss of rendering documentation, although complex real-world NVS remains untested.
